steps_raw.instruction: Slide Preparation for Mounting Samples for TissueCyte 1000 Sectioning and Imaging

Scope and Applicability: This protocol describes the preparation of 1x3 glass slides for mounting embedded mouse brain samples (PF0315: TissueCyte Specimen Embedding - Acrylamide co-embedding) for subsequent imaging and sectioning on TissueCyte 1000 (SOP PF0262: Core Protocol for TissueCyte Serial Imaging).
1x3 glass microscope slides with project-appropriate barcodes
Neodymium magnets, 2.5mm x 2.5mm x 10mm (2 per slide) (Indigo Instruments Product 44226-2.5 or equivalent)
Devcon 5-minute Epoxy Gel (ITW consumer model #21045)
Wooden applicator (Ted Pella Product 128-2 or equivalent)
BULLSEYETM level (Empire level 3604 or equivalent)
Dremel 8200 rotary tool or equivalent
84922 Silicon carbide grinding stone, other Dremel rotary tool accessories that may also be used:
60-grit sanding bands, or
Aluminum oxide graining stone
Sufficiently well-ventilated area; Lab hood, or open workspace
Barcoded 1x3 slides ready for mounting samples for TissueCyte sectioning and imaging.
PF0315: TissueCyte Specimen Embedding - Acrylamide co-embedding
https://www.protocols.io/view/tissuecyte-specimen-embedding-acrylamide-coembeddi-ber4jd8w/abstract
PF0262: Core Protocol for Serial Imaging of Fluorescently-Labeled Mouse Brain on the TissueCyte 1000 System
https://www.protocols.io/view/core-protocol-for-serial-imaging-of-fluorescently-ber7jd9n/abstract

Warning: Personal Protective Equipment () should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what you should be using, see your immediate supervisor. Avoid breathing fumes from Epoxy. Exercise caution when using power equipment (Dremel). Consult your Supervisor or a Health & Safety Officer if you have questions or concerns.
Find a well-ventilated bench area and clear enough work space for the work required.
Many slides can be prepared at one time; plan for appropriate benchtop space requirements ahead of time.
Clear all metals and electronic devices from the bench top where neodymium magnets will be present.
Wipe down benchtop with 70% EtOH to remove dust and dirt.
Obtain all materials necessary and make sure the Dremel is fully charged.
Methodology/Procedures:
Roughen the surface of the front side of the glass slide.
Place a 1x3 slide on a flat surface with the frosted side facing up.
Using the Dremel rotary tool with the appropriate attachment, roughen the surface of the glass slide in the approximate area indicated in Figure 1, lower panel (front side of slide, shaded in blue).
Target area that is approximately 15 mm from the non-painted end of the slide (end with crosshairs); cover whole area from top to bottom of slide, across a width of ~25 mm.
If necessary, draw the target area with a permanent marker on a blank slide and use as a reference.
Set Dremel to medium speed (~40,000 RPM).
Push down on glass lightly to avoid breaking glass.
Roughen the required number of slides one at a time.
Wipe the work surface and glass slides down with 70% ethanol. Make sure that there is no glass dust on the back side of the slides.
Figure 1: Dimensions and layout of slide for specimen mounting
Attach magnets to the back side of the slide
On a clean bench top, separate the individual magnets. Neodymium magnets are extremely strong; they need to be separated at a minimum of 4 cm apart so as to not “strike” each other.
Squeeze a small amount of 5-minute Epoxy on a piece of aluminum foil. Mix the components well with a wooden stick.

Apply a small amount of Epoxy on the backside of the 1x3 slide, 15 mm from the edge of the slide with crosshairs. Visually, the amount of Epoxy should be about the size of the magnet. See Figure 1 for reference.
Do not allow Epoxy to form large globs. Use sparingly.

Using a pair of plastic forceps, place a single magnet in the center of the Epoxy and push down on the magnet as hard as possible, so that magnet is parallel with the glass surface, and aligned perpendicular to the slide edge.
Place the slide to the side to allow the Epoxy to dry. Make sure that the slide is far away from other magnets so that the magnet on the slide does not move before the Epoxy completely hardens.
When making multiple slides at once, repeat steps 8.2.3 – 8.2.5 with other slides. Repeat step 8.2.2 if there is not enough Epoxy or if the Epoxy hardened.
Allow 15-20 minutes for the Epoxy to completely harden. Apply a small amount of Epoxy 20 mm from the first magnet and repeat step 8.2.3 and 8.2.5.
When both magnets are secured, remove excess Epoxy on or around the magnets using a razor blade. It is important that the slide is leveled when placed on a flat surface.
Check that the magnets mounted on each slide align to a level surface by using a small bubble level. If not, discard the slide.
The slides can be stored at room temperature indefinitely in a lint and dust free environment. Slides are ready to be used for PF0315: TissueCyte Specimen Embedding - Acrylamide co-embedding.
Clean work area and put away unused materials.
Dispose of waste in standard non-biohazardous waste stream.
